# SOURCE DOCUMENTS — 2026-08-05 — Do not edit

Five documents sent by the owner on 2026-08-05, transcribed from images. **These supersede
`brother-draft-4-client-model.md` and any part of the build that disagrees with them.**

They are not drafts. They carry a finished logo, a signature block, and the instruction
**"PRICING & SCOPE ARE DONE. DON'T CHANGE IT AGAIN."** Treat them as decided.

Where the build disagreed, the build changed — see `00-model/decisions.md` D-18 through D-24.

**One internal conflict the owner must resolve:** the service agreement says **$279/month**;
the work-block plan and flyer spec say **$249**. Resolved to **$279** on 2026-08-05 (the
agreement is the document a customer signs). $249 also collides with the published `$249+`
grill deep-clean price.

**One date correction:** the agreement is headed *2027 Seasonal Property Care Service
Agreement*, Service Season March 1 – October 31, 2027. The owner is launching **now, in
2026**, so the agreement is re-dated with a partial-season pro-ration clause.

## 2. Service agreement (signed form)

**WESTSIDE PROPERTY CARE 513 — Seasonal Property Care Service Agreement**

Fields: Client · Service Address · Phone / Email · **Service Season: March 1 – October 31**

### 1. Membership & scheduled service
**$279 per month** includes **two scheduled property-care visits each month**, with **up to
two hours of on-site service per visit**. The service is designed to keep outdoor living
areas routinely maintained, clean, functional, and ready to enjoy. **Unused service time does
not roll over.**

### 2. Routine property care
May include: general outdoor-living-area checks; light debris and leaf cleanup in designated
areas; patio and outdoor-space tidying; outdoor countertop and furniture wipe-down; outdoor
trash-can emptying and light wipe-down; outdoor kitchen upkeep; grill exterior and
cooking-area maintenance; grease-trap or drip-pan emptying when appropriate; collection of
sticks and small storm debris; watering outdoor flower pots when requested; basic visual
checks of outdoor equipment and amenities; and notification of observed maintenance concerns.

### 3. Basic pool care
When applicable, may include: surface skimming; brushing steps, corners, and selected areas;
**vacuuming for up to approximately 30 minutes per visit**; emptying skimmer and pump baskets
when safely accessible; emptying automatic pool-vacuum debris containers when applicable;
**backwashing when appropriate and compatible with the system**; visual equipment checks;
**checking displayed salt levels or system indicators**; and notification of visible equipment
warnings.

> **WPC513 does not guarantee water chemistry, water clarity, equipment performance, or
> pool-system operation unless separately contracted.**

### 4. Outdoor kitchen & grill care
Wiping countertops and accessible surfaces; light cleaning around cooking equipment; removal
of accessible grease or food residue; grease-trap or drip-pan emptying when appropriate;
general visual inspection. **Professional grill deep cleaning, repairs, replacement parts,
restoration, and equipment disassembly are not included** and may be quoted separately.

### 5. Service priorities
The Client may identify preferred recurring priorities. Because each visit is limited to
approximately two hours, WPC513 will use reasonable judgment to address the **highest-priority
maintenance items first**. **Completion of every possible task during every visit is not
guaranteed.**

### 6. Additional work
**Work beyond the scheduled service time or outside routine service requires Client approval
before additional billable work is performed.** Examples: professional grill deep cleaning,
pressure washing, extensive storm or leaf cleanup, equipment or pool repairs, replacement
parts, landscaping projects, hauling, specialty cleaning, and significant seasonal opening or
closing work.

### 7. Materials, chemicals & parts
The monthly membership primarily covers **scheduled labor and routine care**. Replacement
parts, specialty cleaners, pool chemicals, salt, filters, repair materials, landscaping
materials, and other consumables are additional unless specifically included. Regulated
pesticide or chemical-application services are excluded unless WPC513 holds any licensing
legally required.

### 8. Scheduling & weather
Service is generally provided **twice per month from March through October** on an approximate
recurring schedule. Arrival times may vary because of weather, prior appointments, traffic,
emergencies, or property conditions. Weather-related visits may be moved to the next
reasonably available service date.

### 9. Property access
Client provides reasonable access including gates, outdoor kitchens, pool equipment,
electrical outlets, water sources. **Pets should be secured when necessary for safe service.**

### 10. Existing conditions
WPC513 is not responsible for pre-existing damage, deterioration, hidden defects, improperly
installed equipment, equipment failure, normal wear, or conditions outside its control.
Potential concerns observed during service will be communicated when reasonably practical.

### 11. Payment
The membership fee is **$279 per month** during the March–October service season. Payment is
due according to the billing arrangement established at enrollment. **Past-due accounts may
result in suspension of scheduled service** until the account is current.

### 12. Cancellation
Either party may terminate with **30 days' written notice**. Amounts already earned for
completed service periods remain due. WPC513 may discontinue service for unsafe working
conditions, repeated nonpayment, abusive conduct, unreasonable service expectations, or
conditions outside the agreed scope.

### 13. Agreement
Signature blocks for **Client** and **Westside Property Care 513**, each with a date.

## 3. Field checklist — "2-HOUR RECURRING SERVICE CHECKLIST"

Two pages. Header: *Designed for printed + laminated use with dry-erase marker.*
Fields: Client / Property · Date · Visit.

Footer on both pages, and the best scope line in any of his documents:

> **WPC513 — Maintain everything. Deep-clean nothing unless specifically scheduled.**

| # | Block | Window | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Arrival + property walkthrough | 0:00–0:10 | 10 min |
| 2 | Pool care | 0:10–0:40 | 30 min max |
| 3 | Outdoor kitchen + grill area | 0:40–1:00 | 20 min |
| 4 | Patio + furniture | 1:00–1:20 | 20 min |
| 5 | Property cleanup | 1:20–1:35 | 15 min |
| 6 | Trash + plants + misc. | 1:35–1:45 | 10 min |
| 7 | Flexible priority block | 1:45–1:55 | 10 min |
| 8 | Final walk + documentation | 1:55–2:00 | 5 min |

**1. Arrival + property walkthrough.** Walk outdoor living areas · check storm debris, leaves,
sticks, trash, obvious issues · visually check pool area and equipment · check outdoor kitchen
/ grill area · note anything unusual or requiring customer approval · take quick before photos
where useful.

**2. Pool care.** Skim pool surface · brush steps, corners, selected areas · vacuum as needed,
stop at approximately 30 minutes total pool time · empty skimmer basket · empty pump basket
when appropriate and safe · empty automatic vacuum debris container if applicable · check
displayed salt level / system indicators · check Inspect Cell / No Flow / other visible
warnings · backwash if needed and appropriate for the system · quick visual equipment
inspection.

**3. Outdoor kitchen + grill area.** Wipe countertops and accessible outdoor-kitchen surfaces ·
remove light food / grease buildup · empty grease trap / drip pan when needed · wipe grill
exterior · check cooking area for excessive buildup · look for obvious pest / nesting
activity · note repairs or deep-cleaning needs.

**4. Patio + furniture.** Wipe patio tables · wipe chairs / furniture as needed · straighten
cushions and furniture · wipe frequently used surfaces · remove obvious cobwebs · light
cleanup around seating areas.

**5. Property cleanup.** Collect sticks / small branches · remove concentrated leaf / debris
pockets · pick up visible trash · sweep / blow small designated areas where appropriate ·
check walkways around outdoor living area.

**6. Trash + plants + misc.** Empty designated outdoor trash cans · light wipe-down of cans
when needed · water outdoor flower pots if requested · handle small recurring homeowner
priorities · check previously noted minor issues.

**7. Flexible priority block.** Extra pool attention · heavier debris pocket · outdoor kitchen
/ grill cleanup · furniture / patio detail · plants / seasonal need · small approved
maintenance item.

**8. Final walk + documentation.** Final property walk · return gates / areas as found · take
after photos · record completed services · note repairs / additional-service recommendations ·
send short service summary to customer.

**NOTES / ITEMS TO QUOTE / FOLLOW-UP** — ruled block at the foot of page 2. This is the
project-finding mechanism the whole model depends on.

## 4. Work-block plan

Header: **PRICING & SCOPE ARE DONE. DON'T CHANGE IT AGAIN.**

**1:30–2:30 PM — Website version 1.** Homepage (logo, branding, headline, plan price, Request
Service CTA) · Services (Pool, Outdoor Kitchen, Exterior) · plan page (up to 4 hours, two-visit
structure) · Trust / About (**local, military roots, service, honesty, integrity,
dependability**) · Contact (Request Service button).

> **HOMEOWNER UNDERSTANDS IN 10 SECONDS: WHAT YOU DO → WHO IT'S FOR → PRICE → HOW TO CONTACT YOU.**

**2:30–3:00 PM — Customer intake system.** A WPC513 Google Sheet:

| Lead information | Tracking |
|---|---|
| Name | Lead status |
| Address | Date contacted |
| Neighborhood | Follow-up date |
| Phone | Plan interested in |
| Email | Notes |
| **Pool Y/N** | Customer Y/N |
| **Outdoor Kitchen Y/N** | Start date |
| Monday/Friday preference | Monthly revenue |

**3:00–3:30 PM — Finish the flyer.** *One flyer. No endless redesigns.* WPC513 logo + strong
property image · the plan and its price · Services: Pool \| Outdoor Kitchen \| Exterior ·
website + Request Service CTA.

**3:30–4:00 PM — First sales list + launch prep.** Create first 20 prospects / target
properties · look for **pools, outdoor kitchens, large patios, landscaping, high-value
homes** · write a simple introduction / pitch.

**4:00 PM — STOP. WORK BLOCK DONE. NO EXCEPTIONS.**
